Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Shah, Marta Lopez, Alex Chen, Sam Patel, Lina Gomez, Devon Park

Summary:
Quick internal enablement: practice demo flow, refine messaging vs competitors, tighten answers to latency/cost questions, and collect action items for collateral updates. Role-play two short demo segments.

Topics: Messaging, competitive positioning, demo flow, quantization/batching, role-play

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Okay, hey everyone thanks for coming, um this is our SE enablement, messaging and demo practice. We'll run through a short deck, do two role plays, and capture follow-ups. Priya, you wanna kick off the demo flow?

[00:18] Priya: Yeah sure, I'll start. Hi team, I'm gonna go through the hosted API quickstart and then switch to dedicated and private considerations. Um, note — I'm gonna call out the KV cache, um key value cache, and prefix caching, sometimes the transcript says K V cash so ignore that.

[00:35] Alex: Quick pause — can you state the main opening value prop in one line for sales? Like, what do we lead with vs Anthropic or OpenAI?

[00:44] Priya: Yeah, so one liner: "Redwood makes inference predictable and economical at production scale — same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with strong observability." It's a mouthful but underline predictable, economical, and unified runtime.

[01:05] Jordan: Nice — emphasize predictable latency and cost controls. People ask about cost vs latency tradeoffs all the time. Marta, any messaging tweaks?

[01:15] Marta: I'd suggest two short soundbites: 1) "Production-first inference with cost-aware controls" and 2) "Unified serving across environments so you don't rewrite your app when you move to Private." Also call out audits — SOC 2 and audit logs — that helps procurement.

[01:34] Priya: Good call. I'll add a quick security slide: SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM options, and on-prem package for regulated workloads.

[01:47] Sam: When customers ask about model performance, are we calling out specific throughput numbers or just guidance? Some AEs want hard numbers.

[01:55] Jordan: We should have reference benchmarks but avoid overpromising — say 'typical latency ranges' and link to model catalog for per-model numbers. If they push, suggest a quick benchmark pilot on Dedicated.

[02:10] Priya: Okay demo start — launching a generation request. "SDK snippet: client.generate(...)." Hit enter.

[02:22] [laughter/overlap] Devon: There's like a small audio glitch, transcript might show 'client dot generate dot' as something else.

[02:30] Priya: So the response streams back, we show streaming, function calling example, and then we switch to embeddings for similarity search. Note — show cost per-token guidance and batching suggestions.

[02:48] Jordan: Call out Redwood Optimize: model and quantization recommendations, and batching/caching suggestions that reduce unit cost. That's a big differentiator vs simple hosted APIs.

[03:05] Priya: Role-play 1: Prospect asks "Why not just use OpenAI?"

[03:12] Priya (as SE): "OpenAI is great for fast prototyping — Redwood is about production economics: predictable latency, dedicated capacity for consistent throughput, private deployment for compliance, and tooling to reduce unit cost like quantization and prefix cache."

[03:34] Alex (as buyer): "How much work is Private? Our security team is strict."

[03:41] Priya: "Private's control plane can be customer-managed, we support VPC and on-prem with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. We also provide onboarding and an enterprise support tier. The SE or solutions team can map the network topology with your infra team."

[04:05] Sam: Good but maybe tighten: say "we have a Private package with a managed control plane and on-prem option; typical onboarding timeline is X weeks depending on infra." We should have a range to cite.

[04:20] Marta: Suggest keep a short template: Timeline: 4-8 weeks for VPC; on-prem depends on site readiness. Don't give exact weeks without syncing with PS.

[04:35] Priya: Noted. Role-play 2: performance objection — buyer says "We need <50ms p99 for chat".

[04:42] Priya (as SE): "Depending on model and sequence length, we tune kernels, batching, and KV cache — for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity or edge routing to lowest-latency region. We can run a pilot to measure p99 on your workload."

[05:00] Devon: One nit — customers often want single-digit ms; be honest that for many large LLMs under long contexts that's not realistic without smaller models or distillation. Suggest alternatives: small specialized models, response caching, or token-trimmed prompts.

[05:18] Jordan: Great point. Also call out automatic fallbacks and graceful degradation — if capacity is constrained we can fallback to compatible variants. That's a reliability thing buyers love.

[05:35] Priya: Demo switch: show Dedicated console — autoscaling policy, burst capacity, and commit levels.

[05:50] [00:06:00] Alex: Quick transcription artifact here — it shows 00:06:00 mid-sentence, ignore.

[06:05] Priya: Walkthrough of rollback/rollouts: canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback to lower-cost variants. Show tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdown.

[06:30] Jordan: Ok now let's do a tight five-minute wall-clock role-play where Alex plays the buyer and Priya runs demo. Marta and I will time and give feedback. Try to keep the demo under 5 minutes focusing on the top value props.

[06:45] [10:00] Role-play run (condensed):
Priya: quick intro, code snippet, streaming demo, switch to embeddings, mention cost controls, mention Private and Dedicated, ask for next steps (pilot).

[10:30] Jordan: Feedback: good rhythm, try to reduce jargon, when you say KV cache maybe briefly define — "key-value cache (KV cache) stores past tokens to speed generation)". Also shorten the security slide to one line unless asked.

[10:55] Marta: Competitive talk track: if a buyer asks about hallucinations — emphasize our quality monitoring and evals tooling tied to prompt sets. If they ask about model training, say we recommend model lifecycle and guard rails but not full training — redirect to partners.

[11:20] Sam: AEs want a quick rebuttal for price objections. Any short script?

[11:27] Jordan: Yes: "We help you reduce unit cost through batching, caching, and quantization so TCO is lower at scale; also predictable commits reduce burst cost surprises." Keep it 1-2 sentences.

[11:42] Priya: Quick show of the Optimize recommendations UI — we point to quantization profiles and model suggestions.

[12:00] Alex: What about multi-region routing, can customers route by policy?

[12:06] Priya: Yes, smart routing by policy (latency, cost, region, customer tier) with automated fallback. We'll have a diagram on the slide.

[12:24] Jordan: Ok let's capture common objection scripts: latency vs cost, compliance/on-prem timeline, hallucination/quality, vendor lock-in.

[12:36] Marta: I'll draft a one-pager with bullets for each objection and suggested scripts.

[12:44] [13:00] Role-play two (billing objection):
Buyer: "We can get cheaper tokens elsewhere."
Priya: "At small scale, token price matters; at production scale your TCO includes latency, failures, and engineering time. Redwood reduces those through runtime features and tooling — we can run a pilot to quantify savings on your workload."

[13:35] Jordan: Good. Now let's do a quick walkthrough of the demo script changes Marta requested — highlight where to add the competitive battleground slide and the quantization demo.

[13:50] Priya: I'll add a short interactive example showing quantized model output quality tradeoff: a before/after of latency and tokens.

[14:08] Devon: Remember to caveat quantization: lower precision may affect quality for some models — include recommended models for quantization.

[14:20] Jordan: Yep. Also make sure we don't imply we support every model for certain quant levels. Use 'recommended models' phrasing.

[14:35] Marta: For battlecard, include common competitor rebuttals: OpenAI — fast prototyping but opaque infra; Anthropic — safety story; Cohere — embeddings strength; Replicate — model marketplace. Provide one-liners.

[14:58] Sam: Any requests for new collateral? AEs asked for a short 2-slide cheat sheet.

[15:06] Marta: I'll create a 2-slide cheat sheet: 1) One-liners + objection responses; 2) Demo checklist (timings, slides to skip, key commands).

[15:20] Jordan: Great. Ok final wrap: recap action items and owners. Priya you update demo script and add quantization snippet. Marta you build battlecard and 2-slide cheat sheet. Jordan schedule follow-up role-play.

[15:40] Priya: Sounds good. One more note — when talking to procurement, surface SOC 2, audit logs, and SSO doc links. I'll add link placeholders in the deck.

[15:55] Jordan: Perfect. Any other questions?

[16:05] Lina: Just a small ask — can we get a recording snippet for the demo to use in enablement?

[16:12] Priya: Yep I'll export a 2-minute clip and share.

[16:20] Jordan: Alright thanks everyone — meeting over.
